data.summary: git merge main in a ddflow worktree fires the post-merge hook, which runs 'ddflow pins regenerate --after-merge' with PYTHONPATH of the primary and cwd of the worktree; that spawns 'pytest tests/golden --snapshot-update' (and test_compat_json etc.) as children of the hook, so they inherit the hook's GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE. The fixture repos' 'git init / add README.md / commit init' then act on the WORKTREE: reflog shows 'Test <[REDACTED:email]> merge main: init' x8 (a chain of junk 'init' commits on the branch), README.md replaced by '# proj' and staged, tests/golden snapshots deleted/rewritten. Observed 2026-10-16 in worktree DX-bug-repro-bundle: the hook ran 12+ minutes (pid 2873173 -> pytest tests/golden --snapshot-update) and a later git commit swept the staged README clobber into HEAD. Wanted: pins regenerate (and any hook-run child) must drop GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_PREFIX before spawning pytest, and not run inside a linked worktree's index at all. Repro: in a claimed worktree run 'git merge main' when main moved; watch 'git reflog' and 'git status'. Regression test: run the hook's regenerate with GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE set to a scratch repo and assert that repo is untouched.
data.title: post-merge pins hook leaks GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE into its pytest run and corrupts the worktree

chunk_findings.detail: `recent_events` is the collector that stands in for "the last N ddflow commands of this session," but it projects each event down to only `{"ts", "kind", "subject"}` (typed `list[dict[str, str]]`) and returns no exit code and no output tail. Given a session such as the one described in the intent — e.g. a gate/command run that failed with a traceback and an exit status — the bundle will record only `ts`/`kind`/`subject` for that run, so the exact command's output and its exit code are dropped, which is precisely the information needed to explain a non-reproducing bug (B29667ba4b4). Even if the underlying hook/session events do carry the output and exit status, this collector discards everything but three fields, so the "with exit codes and output tails" requirement cannot be met from this fact collector. It also violates the module's own stated policy at the top of the file ("a fact that cannot be had is `{"unavailable": why}`") by silently substituting a different, lossier fact for the command history rather than marking it unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:recent_events

chunk_findings.detail: `build` only special-cases the two string literals `"off"` and `"full"`; every other value silently falls through to the `basic` shape (`if mode == "full": ... elif test: ...`). There is no validation and `mode_problem` is never called here, so any path that supplies a mistyped or non-string knob reaches it unchecked. Concrete input: an MCP/CLI/config caller passes `capture=True` (a natural JSON boolean) or `[bugs] repro_capture = "ful"`; `mode = mode or cfg.bugs.repro_capture` accepts it, `mode == "off"` and `mode == "full"` are both false, and the bundle is emitted without `item` (so no lease/gate/findings state), without `machine`, without `recent_events`, and with only `{"id": test, "unavailable": "not run: [bugs] repro_capture is basic"}` for `--test`. `store` then records `"mode": True/"ful"` in the bug's link and no error is surfaced anywhere, so a user who asked for (or typo'd toward) full capture gets silently degraded evidence for exactly the flaky/environment-dependent bugs this feature targets. The fix is to reject anything not in `MODES` (or route through `mode_problem`) rather than treating unknown values as `basic`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:build (mode handling)

chunk_findings.detail: The `commands` field is added unconditionally with the text "the agent's latest log events are listed under `recent_events` instead", but `recent_events` is only assigned inside the `if mode == "full":` branch. With `[bugs] repro_capture = "basic"` (or the invalid-mode case above), `build` returns a bundle whose `commands.unavailable` points at a key that is not in the bundle, and `summary`/`shown` will hand that pointer to `bug show` and to the fix task's claim guidance. Concrete reproduction: set `repro_capture = "basic"`, file a bug, run `ddflow --json show <bug>` — the JSON contains `commands.unavailable` telling the reader to look under `recent_events`, and `recent_events` is absent, so the one piece of evidence the message advertises is unreachable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:build (`out["commands"]` vs `recent_events`)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent for this change states the size/redaction/capture knobs are "all overridable by config/CLI/MCP", and enumerates `[bugs].repro_capture` as the primary knob for the feature. Here the new `repro_capture` parameter is declared with `cli_only=True`, which excludes it from the MCP surface (unlike neighbouring params such as `no_fix_task`, which carry no `cli_only`). Given an MCP caller that wants to file `bug found` with `repro_capture="basic"` for one call — a supported override per the intent — there is no parameter to pass it through, so the call silently falls back to the config default `"full"` and stores a larger bundle than requested (or, for `"off"`, stores a bundle at all when the caller asked for none). The same applies to a caller trying to turn capture off when a sensitive incident is being filed over MCP. `repro_cmd` and `test` are reasonably CLI-only (they are CLI actions, "never run"/"run once"), but `repro_capture` is a value knob and should be exposed on the MCP surface to match the stated override matrix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/records.py:196 (Param "repro_capture")

chunk_findings.detail: The new `repro` field was inserted between `upstream_url`'s `#:` doc comment and `upstream_url` itself. `#:` comments are positional: they document the attribute that immediately follows them. As written, the two lines describing `` `bug.reported_upstream`: where the report about this bug went (a ddflow bug filed against ddflow itself)`` now attach to `repro` (whose own `#:` line follows them and also attaches to `repro`), while `upstream_url` — the field that comment is actually about, and which is the field immediately after `repro` — is left undocumented. Anyone generating attribute docs from these annotations, or reading the model, gets a description of the upstream-report destination on the reproduction-bundle field and no description on the upstream-URL field. The fix is to move the `repro` comment/field below the `upstream_url` lines (or place its own `#:` comment directly above `repro` after the upstream comment block).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/records.py:506-510 (Bug.repro / Bug.upstream_url)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_id` is appended to the pytest argv with no `--` separator and no validation, so any value starting with `-` is consumed by pytest as an option instead of a test selector. Given `ddflow bug found --test '--co'` the run collects only, exits 0, and the bundle records `exit_code: 0` with no test executed — i.e. the repro bundle asserts a test passed that was never run. Given `--test '-p arbitrary_module'` pytest imports and loads an arbitrary module as a plugin, executing its top-level code inside the ddflow process (MCP callers can supply this value per the intent's "overridable by config/CLI/MCP"). The recorded `"command": "pytest " + test_id` also misrepresents what was actually executed (`sys.executable -m pytest --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider`), so the entry is not a faithful repro command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:test_run

chunk_findings.detail: When the path is not inside the project, `_rel` returns `path` unchanged, i.e. the absolute filesystem path. `tree()` feeds it both `cwd` and `worktree`, so a session whose worktree lives outside the repo directory (a normal linked-worktree layout, e.g. `[REDACTED:path]`) records `"worktree": "[REDACTED:path]"` and a cwd outside the repo records the same, storing and printing the operator's home path in an evidence blob meant to be shared. This contradicts the function's own stated rationale that "the machine's home directory says nothing a reader needs", and the change otherwise goes out of its way to keep machine-identifying detail (secrets, absolute paths) out of the bundle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:_rel

chunk_findings.detail: `build` unconditionally writes `commands` as a fixed dict carrying the message "ddflow keeps no log of the commands a session ran (no session or hook command log exists); the agent's latest log events are listed under recent_events instead". The stated intent for this change is precisely the opposite: the bundle must carry "the last N ddflow commands of this session with exit codes and output tails (from the session/hook log)". The file already demonstrates that such a log exists and is reachable — `attach` passes `log.read_all()` in and `full` mode consumes it via `F.recent_events(events, cfg.agent.id, b.repro_events)` — yet the command/exit-code/output-tail portion is never derived from those same events; it is a hardcoded refusal in every mode (`off` excepted). Concrete consequence: for the B8843d3c7bd case (reproduced only partly) or the five flaky-test bugs, the operator gets env, tree, config and events, but never the exact ddflow invocation and its exit code that the intent says is the whole point of the "last commands and output" field, and the stored text falsely asserts no such log exists. If the session/hook log genuinely has no command records, the field should say so from the actual data rather than be hardcoded, but as written it guarantees the requirement is never met.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:57 (out["commands"])

chunk_findings.detail: The change marks the `repro_capture` parameter `cli_only=True`, so it exists only on the CLI surface and cannot be supplied by an MCP client (nor by the gate path that reuses the MCP surface). The stated intent for this change is explicit that the repro knobs, including `[bugs].repro_capture = off|basic|full`, are "all overridable by config/CLI/MCP". Given an MCP tool call that files a bug and wants a minimal or no bundle (e.g. repro_capture="off"), the parameter is absent from the MCP schema, so the call silently falls back to the config default `full` and stores a full repro bundle. The same applies to an agent driving the MCP surface that needs to force `basic` in a constrained environment. Either the parameter should not be `cli_only`, or the MCP surface must thread `repro_capture` explicitly; as declared, the MCP override promised by the intent is unreachable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/records.py:187 (Param "repro_capture")

chunk_findings.detail: The knob's default is declared as a TOML literal *string*, `new = '300'` (single-quoted), not the integer `300`. A TOML parser preserves that distinction: `'300'` loads as `str`, whereas the knob is a timeout in seconds and every other consumer of a `_s` knob treats it as a number. When this template is folded into a release and the value reaches the config, `config["bugs"]["repro_test_timeout_s"]` is the string `"300"`; the code path that bounds the `--test ID` pytest run then does the equivalent of `subprocess.run(..., timeout=<value>)`, which raises `TypeError: 'str' object cannot be interpreted as an integer` (or `"300" * 0.9` / `value > cap` fails the same way). So `ddflow bug found --test <id>` cannot run pytest to capture its output tail even though the knob was "added" with a value that looks correct when read as text. Note the sibling fields in the same file (`kind`, `key`, `why`, `impact`) are written as double-quoted strings, so the single-quoting of `new` is not a uniform convention — it silently changes the value's type. The default should be `new = 300` (unquoted) to match the numeric semantics of a seconds timeout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.bugs.repro_test_timeout_s.toml:7

chunk_findings.detail:
The new repro capture is placed *after* the branch that files an upstream-bound bug and returns early, so those bugs are filed with no bundle. In the hunk the code reads:

```python
        out = DD.extend(log, cfg, chk, "bug.found")
    offer = upstream_offer(scope or (held.scope if held else "project"), target)
    return O.ok("bug.found", **{**out.data, **({"offer": offer} if offer else {})})
repro = RB.attach(repo, cfg, st, log, bid, item=item, agent=agent, test=test,
                  repro_cmd=repro_cmd, capture=repro_capture)
```

That branch still writes a real `bug.found` event (`DD.extend(..., "bug.found")`) but returns before `RB.attach` ever runs, so the written payload has no `repro` key, `core/handlers/knowledge.py` leaves `Bug.repro` at `{}`, and consequently `ddflow bug show` prints nothing and `claim`'s `RB.lead_with` has nothing to lead with for that bug. This contradicts the stated requirement that a bundle is collected for a bug filed via CLI/MCP "without being asked"; the input that demonstrates it is exactly the motivating case in the intent (a bug only observable in the gate environment, e.g. B29d63a65a2): filing it through the upstream path silently drops the DDFLOW_*/GATE env dump, the effective-config deltas and the command/output tail that make it reproducible. The capture (or at least the resulting `repro` dict) needs to be computed before this early return, or folded into `out.data` there.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bugs.py (~line 100-103, the `upstream_offer` early return)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_run` executes pytest with `cwd` pinned to `repo`, the project root, but the tree and branch are computed elsewhere from `Path.cwd()` — `tree()` records `cwd`/`worktree` separately from `repo` and computes `in_linked_worktree` as `rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the running cwd differs from `repo`. That comparison is only meaningful if `repo` is the *main* project root and cwd can be a *linked worktree*, which is the normal ddflow per-lease-worktree setup. So in exactly the case this feature exists for, the test is run against a different revision than the one the bug was observed in. Concrete input: an agent working in linked worktree `…/project-fix-x` (branch `fix/x`, where `tests/test_y.py::test_z` was changed) files `ddflow bug found --test tests/test_y.py::test_z --summary …` while `repo` is the main root. `test_run` invokes `python -m pytest --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider -- tests/test_y.py::test_z` with cwd = main root, so pytest collects either nothing ("file or directory not found" / exit 4) or the main-branch version of the file; the recorded `exit_code`/`tail`/`seed_lines` then describe a tree other than the recorded `tree_sha`/`worktree`, which is precisely the "not reproducible / partly reproducible" failure this bundle is meant to eliminate. The collector should run in the session's cwd (or accept the worktree path), not in `repo`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:test_run (`P.capture(argv, timeout=timeout_s, cwd=str(repo))`)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_run` executes pytest with `cwd=str(repo)`, while the rest of the bundle is explicit that the process cwd and the tree it runs in are *not* the same thing as `repo`: `tree()` computes `cwd` from `Path.cwd()`, `worktree` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of that cwd, and `in_linked_worktree` by comparing that toplevel against `Path(repo)`. That comparison only makes sense if `repo` is the main project root and the session can be running in a linked worktree elsewhere — exactly the layout the change is meant to capture ("the cwd, worktree, branch ..."). So when a bug is filed from such a worktree, e.g. main repo at `[REDACTED:path]` and the session cwd at `[REDACTED:path]` (where the failing test and the modified code actually live), `ddflow bug found --item B123 --test 'tests/test_foo.py::test_bar'` records `cwd`/`worktree` pointing at the worktree and `tree_sha` of the worktree's HEAD, but runs pytest in `[REDACTED:path]`, i.e. a different checkout, possibly on a different branch. The bundle then carries a `tail`, `head`, `seed_lines` and `exit_code` describing the main checkout, not the tree the rest of the bundle describes; and if the test id (or its conftest fixtures) only exists in the worktree, pytest exits 4 with "file or directory not found" and the bundle records a failure that cannot be reproduced from the stated cwd. The same mismatch occurs whenever the operator invokes ddflow from a subdirectory of the project and passes a test id relative to that subdirectory, which is resolved against `repo` instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:test_run (cwd=str(repo))

chunk_findings.detail: The only added logic is `d = RB.lead_with(out, ctx.repo, ctx.log.read_all(), a["id"]).data`, and the return value of `lead_with` is discarded except for `.data`. `claim_text` is the builder of the human-readable claim line: the string it returns is assembled from `d['ttl_s']`, `d['heartbeat_s']` and `d['broke']` (the lines below the hunk are unchanged and therefore cannot reference any new bundle key). So for the exact case the intent calls out -- `ddflow task claim <fix-task-id>` for a bug whose fix task is claimed -- the printed line is still `claimed <id> (lease …s, renew every …s)` plus broke entries; the reproduction bundle that `lead_with` "leads with" never reaches the operator, contradicting "claiming the fix task prints it first". The corresponding implementation in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/bug_found.py` shows the intended pattern (the bundle text is spliced into the string that is handed to `c.out`), whereas here nothing assembled into the message is derived from the bundle. Additionally, if `lead_with` builds a fresh Out (the natural reading of a `lead_with(out, …)` helper), `.data` is that new Out's data, not the claim result, and `d['ttl_s']`/`d['heartbeat_s']` (lines 251-252) raise `KeyError` on every claim; the safe rework is to consume the returned Out/text rather than reduce it to `.data`.

The bundle then carries a `tail`, `head`, `seed_lines` and `exit_code` describing the main checkout, not the tree the rest of the bundle describes; and if the test id (or its conftest fixtures) only exists in the worktree, pytest exits 4 with "file or directory not found" and the bundle records a failure that cannot be reproduced from the stated cwd. The same mismatch occurs whenever the operator invokes ddflow from a subdirectory of the project and passes a test id relative to that subdirectory, which is resolved against `repo` instead.

chunk_findings.detail: The only added logic is `d = RB.lead_with(out, ctx.repo, ctx.log.read_all(), a["id"]).data`, and the return value of `lead_with` is discarded except for `.data`. `claim_text` is the builder of the human-readable claim line: the string it returns is assembled from `d['ttl_s']`, `d['heartbeat_s']` and `d['broke']` (the lines below the hunk are unchanged and therefore cannot reference any new bundle key). So for the exact case the intent calls out -- `ddflow task claim <fix-task-id>` for a bug whose fix task is claimed -- the printed line is still `claimed <id> (lease …s, renew every …s)` plus broke entries; the reproduction bundle that `lead_with` "leads with" never reaches the operator, contradicting "claiming the fix task prints it first". The corresponding implementation in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/bug_found.py` shows the intended pattern (the bundle text is spliced into the string that is handed to `c.out`), whereas here nothing assembled into the message is derived from the bundle. Additionally, if `lead_with` builds a fresh Out (the natural reading of a `lead_with(out, …)` helper), `.data` is that new Out's data, not the claim result, and `d['ttl_s']`/`d['heartbeat_s']` (lines 251-252) raise `KeyError` on every claim; the safe rework is to consume the returned Out/text rather than reduce it to `.data`.
